card.name: Adverbs before encouraged or recommended
card.fires_on: The word "strongly" (and sometimes "is") right before "encouraged" or "recommended", where a label urges an action. Seen mostly in the opioid REMS passage for healthcare providers.

modes.label: strongly before encouraged
modes.description: The adverb "strongly" after "are", ahead of "encouraged to" in a provider-education statement.
modes.example: Healthcare providers are<< strongly>> encouraged to do all of the following:

modes.label: is before recommended
modes.description: The verb "is" just before "recommended" in a monitoring advice sentence.
modes.example: Obtaining an ECG before beginning lacosamide and after lacosamide is titrated to steady-state maintenance dose<< is>> recommended in patients with underlying proarrhyth

card.writes: It pushes the next word toward recommend-type words such as recommended, advisable and 建议.
card.plain: It fires on the word just before a label says something is encouraged or recommended.
